procedural_history.originating_court: Trial Court (inferred from High Court appeal)
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 14.12.2016 of the High Court of Judicature at Madras in CRA No.400 of 2016.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Judicature at Madras, in Criminal Appeal No. 400 of 2016, confirmed the appellant's conviction under the POCSO Act, acquitted the appellant from the charge under Section 366 of the IPC, set aside the sentence for that charge, and reduced the sentence of life imprisonment with rigorous imprisonment to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment. The appellant was also convicted under Section 10 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant appealed to the Supreme Court, and the Supreme Court allowed the appeal.

directions: The appellant shall be set at liberty forthwith unless required in connection with any other case.

issue.issue_text: Whether the judgment of the High Court confirming the appellant's conviction and sentence should be set aside.

facts: The appellant was convicted by the High Court under Section 6 of the POCSO Act and Section 10 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.
The High Court had already acquitted the appellant of the charge of kidnapping under Section 366 of the IPC.
The victim (M) changed her version and deposed in court contrary to her earlier statement made under Section 164 of the Cr.PC.
The prosecution did not provide any evidence to establish that the victim's age was under 18.
law: To sustain a conviction under the POCSO Act, the prosecution must prove that the victim was a minor (under 18 years old) at the time of the alleged offence.
Significant contradictions in the testimony of the primary witness (the victim) can weaken the prosecution's case.
An acquittal on a related charge, such as kidnapping, can undermine the overall credibility of the prosecution's narrative.
application: The Court found the prosecution's case to be critically flawed due to its failure to provide any evidence proving the victim was a minor, a fundamental requirement for a POCSO conviction.
The Court considered the totality of the circumstances, including the fact that the victim had changed her testimony, which cast doubt on the reliability of the prosecution's story.
The Court noted that the appellant's acquittal on the kidnapping charge (Section 366 IPC) contradicted the prosecution's theory of a forceful abduction, further weakening the case against him.
reasoning.conclusion: Based on the prosecution's failure to prove the victim's age, the victim's contradictory statements, and the prior acquittal on the kidnapping charge, the Supreme Court concluded that the appellant was not guilty. Consequently, it set aside the High Court's judgment, acquitted the appellant of all charges, and allowed the appeal.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the judgment of the High Court confirming the appellant's conviction and sentence should be set aside.
appellant_arguments: The trial court's approach was entirely erroneous because its finding was that the prosecution was unable to show that a witness (M) was not under some coercion from the appellant.

This reasoning is illogical because when the Magistrate recorded the witness's statement, the witness was clearly not under the influence of the appellant, and the Magistrate had recorded an opinion to this effect.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: An order made by a Special Court regarding the age of a person, as determined under the relevant sub-section, shall not be deemed invalid merely by any subsequent proof that the determined age was incorrect.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court concluded that the appellant's conviction was unsustainable because it was based on the trial court's entirely erroneous and illogical reasoning. The trial court incorrectly discarded the victim's in-court testimony (where she did not support the prosecution) based on its finding that the prosecution could not prove she was free from the appellant's coercion. This reasoning was flawed, especially since the evidence clearly indicated the victim's willingness to accompany the appellant and marry him.
